hooks.text: Only three people in history have died in space.
A Soviet capsule landed perfectly, but everyone inside had died.
Why have only three people ever died beyond our atmosphere?

title: The Only Humans to Die in Space
description: In 1971, three Soviet cosmonauts lost their lives returning from the world's first space station. This is the tragic story of Soyuz 11.

beats.text: Only three people in history have died in space.
beats.visual: illustration of the Soyuz 11 descent module drifting in low Earth orbit, 1971

beats.text: In June 1971, three Soviet cosmonauts docked with Salyut 1, the world's first crewed space station.
beats.visual: photograph of the Salyut 1 space station in Earth orbit, 1971

beats.text: After more than three weeks of orbital experiments, their Soyuz 11 spacecraft undocked to return to Earth.
beats.visual: photograph of the Soyuz 11 cosmonaut crew inside the Salyut 1 space station, 1971

beats.text: Roughly 80 to 100 miles above Earth, capsule separation accidentally jarred open an air equalization valve.
beats.visual: diagram showing the separation of the Soyuz descent and service modules, 1971

beats.text: The cabin depressurized into space in less than one minute, with the crew wearing no pressurized spacesuits.
beats.visual: technical diagram of the Soyuz pressure equalization valve assembly, 1971

beats.text: Yet the automated ship guided itself home, surviving re-entry and touching down on parachutes in Kazakhstan.
beats.visual: photograph of the charred Soyuz 11 descent module on the Kazakh steppe, 1971

beats.text: Rescuers opened the hatch expecting triumphant record-breakers, but found all three cosmonauts dead in their seats.
beats.visual: photograph of recovery personnel inspecting the landed Soyuz 11 capsule, 1971

beats.text: A single open valve had sealed their tragic place in history.
beats.visual: photograph of state funeral portraits of the three Soyuz 11 cosmonauts, 1971

better_than_last: Applies the ep084 and ep114 learnings by avoiding verbatim hook repetition in the final beat while maintaining a seamless loop back to the opening statement.
